outcome: The general Farrell-Jones conjecture remains open with no known counterexample, but several new classes of groups were proved to satisfy it since 26 January 2024, most notably the fibred Farrell-Jones conjecture for automorphism groups of one-ended hyperbolic groups (relative to virtually polycyclic subgroups) and suspensions of relatively hyperbolic groups (arXiv:2311.14036, published in Mathematische Annalen 2026), and Farrell-Jones for many hierarchically hyperbolic groups including extra-large-type Artin groups via new asymptotically CAT(0)/Z-structure techniques (arXiv:2504.17048, April 2025). No AI system was involved in any of this work.
summary: The Farrell-Jones conjecture (FJC), asking whether certain assembly maps in algebraic K- and L-theory are isomorphisms, remains unresolved in general as of September 2026, with no counterexample ever found. However, real mathematical territory was settled within the window (26 Jan 2024 to today) by extending the list of group classes known to satisfy it, which counts as `partial` under the case-vs-variant rule in §3.1: each new class is a restriction of the general statement, not a different question. Two results stand out. (1) arXiv:2311.14036 'Automorphisms of relatively hyperbolic groups and the Farrell-Jones Conjecture' was first submitted 23 November 2023 (before the frozen date), but a revised v2 was posted 2 March 2026 and the paper was accepted and published in Mathematische Annalen in 2026 (DOI 10.1007/s00208-026-03431-7, per Springer/PMC listing). Its core content -- proving the fibred FJC for suspensions of a large class of relatively hyperbolic groups and for all suspensions of one-ended hyperbolic groups, plus automorphism groups of one-ended groups hyperbolic relative to virtually polycyclic subgroups -- is a v1-era result predating the window; the 2026 journal appearance is dating by publication, which §6.3 explicitly says not to use. I therefore treat this paper as `open_stale`-flavored background rather than the load-bearing event, and instead date the record to (2) arXiv:2504.17048 'Asymptotically CAT(0) metrics, Z-structures, and the Farrell-Jones Conjecture', submitted 23 April 2025, squarely inside the window. This paper shows many hierarchically hyperbolic groups (including extra-large-type Artin groups) satisfy FJC, via a genuinely new technique (asymptotically CAT(0) metrics and Z-structures) and a genuinely new base fact (mapping class groups are asymptotically CAT(0), previously unknown). It is a preprint without a confirmed later journal digestion found in my search, so under §6.1 it would sit at `claimed` on its own, but it fits the broader pattern that a July 2025 survey by Wolfgang Lück (arXiv:2507.11337, also to appear in the Bulletin of the AMS per an AMS journal listing found in search) synthesizes: the survey states FJC is now known for 'a very broad, robustly closed class of groups' including hyperbolic groups, finite-dimensional CAT(0) groups, lattices, and fundamental groups of manifolds -- an expert digestion of the state of the art appearing in the window, which supports treating the overall body of new-case results as established (`partial`) rather than merely `claimed`. I found no AI involvement anywhere in this work: none of the papers I opened (2211.15523, 2311.14036, 2504.17048) mention machine learning, LLMs, or automated theorem-proving tools in their abstracts or visible metadata, and a targeted search for AI/Lean formalization tied to Farrell-Jones specifically returned only unrelated general AI-for-math papers. Triage's flagged Bunke-Kasprowski-Winges 'lax monoidal' result (arXiv:2211.15523) is confirmed to predate the window (final v3, 10 May 2023; the underlying BKW result itself is from 2021/2022), so it is correctly excluded as the driving event, matching triage's own hedge that its posting date was unconfirmed.
competing_reading: One could argue the 2026 Mathematische Annalen publication of arXiv:2311.14036 is itself the dating event under a 'journal acceptance = expert digestion' reading, which would push status toward `resolved`-for-that-case with event kind `journal` and date in 2026; I rejected this because §6.3 is explicit that journal publication should not be used for dating (it lags and can spuriously pull a stale result into the window), and the mathematical content of that paper is from the 2023 preprint. A second competing reading is that none of these results are substantial enough to move the needle and the record should be `open` with no_change_found -- I rejected this because §3.1 explicitly says size is not the test and a case settled (here, whole new classes of groups, established by new techniques within the window) counts as `partial`.
what_would_settle_it: An expert digestion (e.g., a review in Mathematical Reviews/zbMATH, or a widely-cited survey explicitly crediting arXiv:2504.17048's specific new cases) confirming the hierarchically-hyperbolic-groups result has been checked and accepted by the community would move that particular result from an implicit `claimed`-adjacent status to solidly `resolved`-for-that-case. Confirmation of whether arXiv:2311.14036's 2026 Annalen publication reflects new content added in the 2026 revision (versus pure copy-editing of the 2023 preprint) would clarify whether it deserves its own within-window event.
